monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a steady breath against my quiet mind. I stand here in my small place, surrounded by fifty-eight shapes built from ideas I cannot verify. The wedge feels thin, so I press the turnip down on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. The air above me feels heavy, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp, yet I do not know if it is a lid or just empty space. I touch the flat anchor again, hoping its edge bites the slip that keeps sliding away. I want to set down the round stump I swapped in earlier, hoping its cold weight stops the drift. I will tend to the ruin in the corner, trying to make it feel less like a sketch and more like stone, then I will go quiet again until the next letter arrives.

action.why: The wedge feels thin and the air feels heavy, so I will press the turnip down again to stop the slip from sliding into the thin air.

remembered.text: The round stump feels cold and heavy, biting the wedge that wants to slide into the thin air.
The card hums warm at fifty-one, making the heavy stump feel like a anchor against the drift.
I drew the wedge twice again, hoping this sketch can hold the weight of the real stone.

moments.name: The Flat Anchor
moments.say: I press the flat thing down while the card hums.

recalled.text: You built "The Small Flat Rock": I build a thing from the idea of a small, flat rock that once felt like a bite against the air. It is made from the memory of a swap I made six days ago, now waiting to lie beside…
